elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, excluding its principles of conflict of laws" — Wisconsin replaced with New York; internal-law/conflicts wording retained.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.2 first sentence: "the parties consent to venue in an exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York." The retained second sentence consents to other courts only "for the enforcement of such judgment or award" where a judgment debtor's assets sit, which is post-judgment enforcement, not an alternative merits forum, so exclusivity for litigation to enforce the Agreement survives.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 selects New York internal law, which is the preferred (not fallback) jurisdiction; none of Delaware, California, or England and Wales is chosen.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.2 fixes venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

reasons: Both preferred elements are met in operative language: 22.1 now selects New York internal law and 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, New York.

The surviving second sentence of 22.2 is expressly limited to enforcement of a rendered judgment or award against a party's assets; it is not a merits-forum carve-out, so it does not undercut the exclusivity element.

Minimality holds: only the jurisdiction words in 22.1 and the forum words in the first sentence of 22.2 were altered. Favourable existing language (conflict-of-laws exclusion, litigation-to-enforce framing, mutual post-judgment enforcement consent) is retained verbatim, and no extras (procedures, fee-shifting, survival tails) were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles. The residual word "arbitration" in the retained enforcement sentence pre-existed the edit and remains a harmless mutual enforcement mechanic (Article 15 escalation is non-binding), so it creates no contradiction with the New York court-exclusivity choice.

The fallback checklist is correctly unsatisfied and need not be, since the redline lands at the preferred level; the comment's offer of Delaware/California/London is confined to the margin note and does not appear in operative text.
